newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends higher, extends Monday gain.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends higher, extends Monday gain.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures ended higher Tuesday as shortcovering extended Monday's gain.
Stronger cash power prices in the western U.S. and a continued rebound in natural gas futures also pushed the complex higher, market sources said.
March California-Oregon Border (COB) futures finished up 24 cents at $11.12 a megawatt hour (MWh) after trading between $11.00 and $11.45. April COB ended up 20 cents at $10.25.
March Palo Verde (PV) futures finished up 52 cents at $13.65 after posting a session high of $13.75. April PV ended up 20 cents at $12.30.
Day-ahead firm, peak electricity at COB and PV rose 50 to 75 cents today.
NYMEX March Henry Hub natural gas futures settled up 18.4 cents at $2.497 per million British thermal units.
Swing natgas deliveries at the San Juan Hub in New Mexico were again quoted near $2.30/mmBtu.

Despite the complex's two-day rise, most participants remained bearish about the prospect of the power contracts due to mounting evidence of strong runoffs and record snowpack for hydroelectric output through the spring, market sources said.
"There's a little more room to firm, but it would eventually soften again," said a Denver-based trader.

In the Pacific Northwest, temperatures were forecast to be near normal through Thursday before falling to two to four degrees below normal Friday. Variable clouds with a chance of rain was expected in the region for the rest of the week.
In the Southwest, temperatures were called to remain above normal into next week with normal precipitation across California and Nevada and above-normal precipitation elsewhere.
A 1,100 megawatt (MW) pumped storage hydroelectric plant near Fresno, Calif., was shut last Saturday for mechanical repairs, and could stay down for up to two weeks.
Restart of the 790 MW unit 1 at the Mohave coal-fired power plant was postponed to Wednesday from today. The unit near Laughlin, Nev., was shut Friday due to a tube leak.
The 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant at Richland, Wash., was running at 59 percent power amid ongoing work on its recirculation pumps.
NYMEX estimated 655 COB and 231 PV contracts were sold, up from Monday's trade of 246 COB and 105 PV.
